name: Autochrome Orchard

credits: Glaze original built-in image_gen nature artwork and authored live native identity. Autochrome-inspired digital colour photography.
prompt: Use case: natural botanical and wildlife artwork. GLAZE AUTOCHROME ORCHARD. ONE familiar real nature subject with true natural anatomy and tissue, photographed as a beautiful EARLY ADDITIVE-COLOUR AUTOCHROME-INSPIRED POSITIVE IMAGE. The visibly distinctive photographic language is a fine RANDOM MULTICOLOURED STARCH-SCREEN GRAIN across the actual image tones: tiny irregular red-orange, muted leaf-green and blue-violet colour-filter specks combine into a soft natural-colour photographic image. At1024resolution the irregular speckles are mostly2to6pixels, dense but fine, uneven and subtly chromatic, never a regular screen grid or large colored cells. Photographic image structure and silhouette stay fully continuous and recognisable beneath this fine additive colour screen. The optical grain is flat image texture, NOT physical grains, coloured skin patches, a coat of sand or body construction. Soft pictorial photographic focus with clearly resolved whole silhouettes, gently muted rose, faded cornflower blue, sage green, buttercream and warm amber shadows. Delicate luminous low-contrast colour-positive feel, slight honey colour bias, fine multicoloured mottled grain visible in light and midtone areas. Real natural subject, not an illustration, painterly brushstrokes, coarse print, screenprint, risograph dots, half-tone ink, pixel art, mosaic body, orientation map, beads, sand sculpture, physical film ribbons or perforated frames. No duplicated/ghost exposures, neon, fluorescence, transmitted-vein glow, glass/plastic organisms or magical aura. No heavy antique scratches, fading holes, damage, torn edges or plate rectangle. No letters, numbers, labels, reading, UI, watermark or logo.
